title: Erumely's pristine pine forest all set to become next eco-tourism hotspot
content: Erumely's Kanakappalam forest division is home to a breathtaking stretch of pine trees, sparking local demands to transform the area into a major leisure and tourism hub. Planted and nurtured under the Kerala Forest Department, this lush green canopy bears a striking resemblance to the famous pine valleys of Vagamon. However, unlike Vagamon's characteristic chilly high-altitude climate, Kanakappalam offers a more moderate, pleasant atmosphere, making it highly accessible for casual day-trippers.Adjacent to this natural pine grove, a government-constructed pond adds to the scenic charm of the location. Local residents point out that the town and its surrounding areas currently lack well-equipped recreational spaces. Developing the forest zone with family-oriented amenities, seating areas, and a children's park would not only address this gap but also generate sustainable livelihood opportunities for the local community.Proposed plans and eco-friendly development To unlock the full potential of the site, community leaders and visitors have emphasised the need for proper vehicle parking and basic infrastructure. Clearing the undergrowth and installing eco-friendly benches would immediately make the space a popular evening and weekend retreat for families. Responding to these demands, Forest Department officials have indicated that a comprehensive development plan is in the pipeline. The proposed eco-tourism initiative aims to actively involve local communities in managing the destination, ensuring that environmental conservation goes hand-in-hand with sustainable tourism development.
